subject: Post-demo: StratusCloud inference comparison & next tests
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@stratuscloud.com>, Priya Shah <priya@stratuscloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: StratusCloud inference comparison & next tests

Hi Alex / Priya — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Recap:
- Main ask: quantify runtime cost and p95 latency across your typical workloads vs your current hyperscaler setup (Vertex/Bedrock) and vs Redwood hosted/dedicated.
- Key constraints: 95th latency target <= 200ms for short chat flows, ability to hit steady-state 200 QPS for medium workloads, and predictable unit economics for billing.

Immediate asks (can you confirm answers / data for these?):
1) Typical per-request token distribution (we need short/median/long buckets). Example: 1) <=128 tokens, 2) 256–512, 3) >1024.
2) Current observed cache hit rates for prompt prefixes / system messages (ballpark %).
3) Any model variants you’re testing (e.g., 70B/13B, quantized FP16/INT8).
4) Acceptance criteria for a short canary (latency SLO, error budget, sample throughput).

Proposed next tests (we can run these with a small dataset you share):
- Test matrix: short/medium/long sequences, batch sizes {1, 4, 16}, KV caching enabled vs disabled, and measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
- Redwood will run a mirrored job against our hosted endpoint + a dedicated-reserved config to show delta.

Quick ballpark (for planning only):
- Redwood hosted: ~ $22 per 1M tokens for the model class we demoed (with typical caching ~30% effective token reduction).
- Hyperscaler (your reported Vertex/Bedrock baseline): ~$38–45 per 1M tokens for comparable throughput under small-batch settings (no KV caching).
- Dedicated reserved: could drop to ~$10–14 per 1M tokens depending on commit and batching.

Attachments: redwood-cost-estimate-1M.xlsx (workup), stratus-test-matrix.csv (proposed matrix).

Next steps:
- Can you send a 200–500 sample session logs (anonymized) or a token distribution summary?
- I’ll schedule a 30-min run-planning call this week to lock the test window.

If it helps, we can also include a lightweight client-side harness (Python) so you run the same payloads against your current setup.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
From: Alex Porter <aporter@stratuscloud.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya@stratuscloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 17:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: StratusCloud inference comparison & next tests

Thanks Sean — good summary. A couple quick clarifications and data points from our side:

1) Token distribution (rough): short (~45% of calls, median 60 tokens), medium (~40%, median 420 tokens), long (~15%, avg 1,500 tokens).
2) Current prefix cache hit rate: ~18% (we do some client caching but not universal).
3) Models: primary is a 70B FP16; we’ve been experimenting with 13B INT8 for cost-sensitive flows.
4) Our current per-1M token bill (Vertex + custom infra): around $40–44 depending on steady-state. That includes data egress and orchestration overhead.

We can provide 250 anonymized session logs (ready by Wed). Agree on the matrix; also want to measure end-to-end tail latency (client -> model -> post-process).

On your ballpark numbers: those look promising. For the dedicated pricing, can you confirm assumed sustained utilization (e.g., 60% vs 90%) and whether the numbers include amortized monitoring/trace costs?

We’d be happy to run the client harness. Let’s tentatively set the run-planning slot for Wed 10:00 PT if that works.

— Alex
Alex Porter
Director of ML Platform, StratusCloud
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@stratuscloud.com>, Priya Shah <priya@stratuscloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: StratusCloud inference comparison & next tests

Alex — perfect, thanks for the numbers. Short replies and a proposed test plan + assumptions: 

Assumptions for our dedicated numbers: sustained utilization = 70% over a 30-day window, includes basic observability (retention tier 30d) but excludes expensive long-term storage and third-party tracing fees. We’ll annotate total cost and a line for "full-stack" add-ons.

Proposed test timeline / matrix (attached stratus-test-matrix.csv):
- Day 0: kickoff & environment verification, upload sample logs
- Day 1: short sequences (<=128) — batch sizes 1,4,16; KV cache off/on
- Day 2: medium sequences (~512) — batch 1,4,8; measure p95 and tokens/sec
- Day 3: long sequences (>1024) — single dedicated runs to measure memory pressure and tail

Metrics we’ll capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens generated / second, costed tokens (after cache hits), and end-to-end client latency.

Proposed acceptance for canary: p95 <= 200ms for short flows, error rate < 0.5% and sustained throughput within 10% of target. If Stratus signs a 3-month dedicated pilot, we can provide a $10k trial credit to offset evaluation costs and a one-week free warm-up (no usage invoiced).

Attachments: rdw-trial-agreement.pdf (sample), redwood-cost-estimate-1M.xlsx (detailed math).

I’ll bring Monica (ops lead) on the run planning call to align on infra and onboarding. Wed 10:00 PT works for me — sending calendar now.

Best — Sean
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Alex Porter <aporter@stratuscloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya@stratuscloud.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 12:44:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: StratusCloud inference comparison & next tests

Quick internal note and request (cc’ing the customer to keep transparency):

- For the test runs, please include model variant tags and quantization settings in the payload metadata (e.g., model=rw-70b-fp16, quant=int8). That lets us normalize latency/cost per variant.
- We should also capture cache key cardinality and average KV object size (KB) per session — this materially affects memory footprint and effective hit rate.
- If Stratus can enable a small sample run with INT8 13B that will help show the cost/latency tradeoff clearly.

I’ll stand by to validate the run outputs and annotate the cost sheet with quantization/throughput multipliers.

— Neha (on infra/econ)
From: Alex Porter <aporter@stratuscloud.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 10:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: StratusCloud inference comparison & next tests

Thanks everyone — we’re good to proceed. I’ve attached the anonymized 250 sessions (zipped) to the calendar event and confirmed Wed 10:00 PT for kickoff. A couple final items:

- We’d like Redwood to include a short column in the run output with an estimated $/1M tokens per-row so we can map cost to specific flows.
- For the dedicated estimate, please include both 70% and 90% sustained utilization rows; we’ll use both to model procurement talk tracks.

Alex
Alex Porter
Director of ML Platform, StratusCloud
